title: Distributed synthesis of arbitrary graph states in quantum networks via rank-two GF(2) reduction
authors: Xiaoyi Zheng, Lin Chen, Chan-Tong Lam
abstract: Existing schemes for synthesizing graph states in quantum networks are essentially edge-by-edge constructions, so quantities such as the time-slot depth and the resource overhead grow significantly with the edge density of the target graph. This paper proposes a new method. Exploiting the mathematical equivalence between joint Pauli-X measurements and graph pivot operations, we formulate graph state synthesis as a rank-2 reduction process of a difference matrix over GF(2), and give an upper bound floor(N/2) on the number of steps for synthesizing an arbitrary N-node graph state, independent of the edge density of the target graph state. At the physical level, the joint Pauli-X measurement of each step is mapped to a dual-star concurrent distribution. We model the protocol on Waxman physical topologies with fiber attenuation and give a heuristic algorithm, and evaluate it against a strengthened Steiner baseline through Monte Carlo experiments. The experimental results show that our protocol is superior in time-slot depth almost everywhere. The entanglement resource overhead, the total number of CZ gates, and the number of Pauli measurements drop below the baseline near edge density p approximately 0.3, and are superior across the board thereafter. The denser the target graph state, the more significant the advantage.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, algebraically grounded method to synthesize arbitrary graph states in quantum networks by framing the process as a rank-2 reduction over GF(2). By mapping this to a dual-star concurrent distribution on a physical network model, the authors demonstrate a protocol that significantly reduces resource overhead and time-slot depth compared to existing edge-by-edge constructions, especially for dense target graphs.
main_problem: Existing methods for synthesizing graph states in quantum networks suffer from resource overhead that scales poorly with the edge density of the target graph.
main_result: The proposed rank-2 reduction method achieves a step count upper-bounded by floor(N/2), independent of edge density, and outperforms existing baselines in time-slot depth and resource overhead for dense graphs.
method: The synthesis problem is reformulated as a rank-2 reduction process of a difference matrix over GF(2), which is physically mapped to a dual-star concurrent entanglement distribution.
model_or_system: The work models quantum networks using Waxman physical topologies with fiber attenuation, simulating the process using a time-slot model.
key_observables: Time-slot depth, entanglement resource overhead (CZ gates, Pauli measurements), and total number of steps.
important_parameters: Edge density (p), number of nodes (N), and the physical attenuation parameters of the network.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the equivalence between joint Pauli-X measurements and graph pivot operations, and the time-slot model assumes classical information transfer within one slot.
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of the proposed protocol against a strengthened Steiner baseline across varying edge densities (p), showing the divergence in step count and total depth, and the crossover point where the proposed method surpasses the baseline in resource overhead.
paper_structure: The paper reviews graph state theory and its GF(2) representation, establishes the rank-2 synthesis framework, details the physical mapping and heuristic algorithm, and concludes with Monte Carlo numerical results comparing performance metrics.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, resource-aware protocol for preparing complex quantum states in realistic network models, directly impacting the feasibility of large-scale quantum computation architectures.
